title: Baked Custard with Oats
subtitle: A creamy baked oat custard with nutmeg and honey
excerpt: This is a slow-baked egg custard with a layer of rolled oats that softens into the base as it cooks. It is simple, filling, and makes a good breakfast or pudding. The texture is somewhere between a baked custard and a rice pudding.
sourceNotes: Baked egg custards are one of the oldest sweet dishes in European cooking, found in both British and French traditions. This version adds oats for texture and substance.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Can be made a day ahead and served at room temperature or cold from the fridge.
recipe.temperatureNote: Fan 140C / Gas 3. Low heat is essential for a smooth set.

content.text: Bake this in a bain-marie for the most even, silky set. Place the baking dish inside a larger roasting tin, then pour boiling water into the outer tin to come halfway up the sides of the dish.
Butter a deep baking dish (about 1.5 litre capacity) generously.
Spread the oats in an even layer in the bottom of the dish.
Whisk together the eggs, egg yolks, cream, milk, honey, and nutmeg until smooth.
Pour the custard mixture over the oats. Let it sit for 5 minutes to start soaking in.
Place the baking dish inside a larger roasting tin. Pour boiling water into the outer tin until it reaches halfway up the dish.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the custard is just set with a slight wobble in the centre.
Remove from the bain-marie. Allow to cool for 10 minutes before serving.

items.symptom: The custard has curdled and looks grainy.
items.cause: The oven was too hot or there was no water bath.
items.fix: Always use a bain-marie and keep the oven at 160C maximum.

items.symptom: The centre is completely liquid after 40 minutes.
items.cause: Oven temperature was too low or the dish was very deep.
items.fix: Return to the oven for 10 more minutes and check every 5 minutes.
